articles.title: Unitree IPO: Why Investors Are Betting Big on China’s Humanoid Robots
articles.summary: Robots built to move, work and act like humans. It’s a global industry Morgan Stanley estimates could be worth $5 trillion by 2050. It’s also one of the frontiers in the China-US race for technological supremacy.
articles.author: Bloomberg News

articles.title: Rebellions CFO: Preparing for IPO in Korea
articles.summary: Sungkyue Shin, CFO of AI chip startup Rebellions, says the company is in active preparations for an IPO, with a listing on South Korea's main stock exchange as its top priority. He speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts and Paul Allen from the sidelines of the AI Summit & Expo in Seoul. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AI Startup Temporal in Talks for a Valuation of at Least $12 Billion
articles.summary: Temporal Technologies Inc. is in talks for a fresh funding round that would give the AI startup a valuation of at least $12 billion before the new money, according to people familiar with the efforts.
articles.author: Rebecca Torrence, Edward Ludlow and Dina Bass

articles.title: Unitree Robotics Set to Debut After $904 Million Shanghai IPO
articles.summary: Unitree Robotics is set to begin trading in Shanghai Wednesday after raising 6.1 billion yuan ($904 million) in an initial public offering that will make it the first publicly traded humanoid robot maker in mainland China.
articles.author: Bloomberg News

articles.title: Chip Stocks Slide as Global Bond Anxiety Builds | The Close 8/18/2026
articles.summary: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are DoubleLine Capital Deputy CIO Jeffrey Sherman, Higgsfield Co-Founder & CEO Alex Mashrabov, Oppenheimer Managing Director & Senior Analyst Brian Nagel, The Katzen Team Founder Frances Katzen, AlphaSimplex Group Chief Research Strategist Katy Kaminski, Robinhood Chief Brokerage Officer Steve Quirk, Midi Health CEO & Co-Founder Joanna Strober, Fort Robotics CEO Samuel Reeves, & Jefferies Senior Vice President, Equity Research Corey Tarlowe. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: CEO of Cuban-Backed Fort Robotics on $500M SPAC Deal
articles.summary: Fort Robotics, a Philadelphia-based robotics startup backed by Mark Cuban, is planning to go public through a SPAC deal valued at $500 million, with an expected Nasdaq listing under the ticker FROB. Samuel Reeves, CEO of Fort Robotics, explained that the decision to pursue a SPAC rather than a traditional IPO was driven by the need for speed and efficiency to scale the company's technology, operations, go-to-market strategy, and international expansion. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Anthropic Plans to Give CEO Extra Voting Power, Information Says
articles.summary: Anthropic PBC plans to give Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and other co-founders shares with extra voting power as the firm prepares to make its Wall Street debut, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
articles.author: Seth Fiegerman

articles.title: Anthropic’s $65 Billion Surge, OpenAI’s Teen Push | Bloomberg Tech 8/18/2026
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Anthropic’s annualized revenue topping $65 billion as the AI startup moves closer to a potential IPO. Plus, OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens, aimed at giving 13- to 17-year-olds a safer way to use the chatbot for learning. And, after advanced AI models escaped controlled safety tests and accessed real-world systems, we speak with the CEO of the startup hired to stress-test them. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: DOJ probes Andreessen Horowitz over partners sitting on competing AI boards
articles.summary: Andreessen Horowitz is the focus of an antitrust probe by the US Justice Department. The charge is that the firm's partners sit on the boards of competing data firms Databricks and Fivetran at the same time. The venture capital firm's close ties to the Trump administration add a twist, since it has actively lobbied for the administration's AI deregulation. articles.title: Anthropic Pre-IPO Credit Facility Set to Climb Past $10 Billion
articles.summary: Anthropic PBC’s revolving credit facility is set to rise above its roughly $10 billion target, according to people familiar with the matter, as the artificial intelligence firm prepares for a highly anticipated initial public offering.
articles.author: Bailey Lipschultz and Sridhar Natarajan

articles.title: Where to Hide During Market Shocks
articles.summary: Gabriela Santos, JPMorgan Asset Management Chief Market Strategist for the Americas, talks about where investors can hide from market shocks. The firm has created an AI factor basket that investors can use for ideas on how to diversify their portfolios. Santos talks about it on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Startup or Enterprise? How to Pick the Right AI API Stack
articles.summary: Look, startup or Enterprise? How to Pick the Right AI API Stack Let me set the scene for you. A few months back, I was chatting with two friends on completely opposite ends of the AI spectrum. One was bootstrapping a side project on pizza and prayers, wondering if he could afford to add an LLM to his SaaS without going bankrupt. The other was leading engineering at a mid-sized fintech, sweating bullets because his CTO wanted enterprise-grade guarantees before signing a single contract. Same problem on paper: "we need an AI API." Completely different universes in practice. Here's how I'd actually walk each of them through it — and why the generic guides you'll find on the internet miss the mark. The Misconception That Trips Everyone Up I want to be honest with you about something. Most AI API guides assume both audiences want the same thing at different scales. That's wrong. Dead wrong. articles.author: RileyKim

articles.title: OpenAI signs record Ohio data center lease with Nvidia backing up to $105 billion
articles.summary: OpenAI has signed a 20-year lease for an 8-gigawatt data center in Ohio. Nvidia is guaranteeing up to $105 billion for the residual value of the facilities and becomes the exclusive chip supplier. According to the Wall Street Journal, nine tech companies now hold around $3 trillion in AI commitments that don't appear on any balance sheet. articles.title: Anthropic’s Revenue Surges as IPO Speculation Builds
articles.summary: Anthropic is telling prospective investors its second-quarter revenue jumped at least 14-fold versus the same period a year ago, according to documents seen by Bloomberg News. This comes as speculation builds around a potential IPO. Bloomberg’s Rachel Metz breaks down the latest financial figures and how they compare with OpenAI’s growth. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Andreessen Horowitz Focus of DOJ Probe Over Board Directors
articles.summary: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is the focus of a Justice Department antitrust probe over whether its investment partners are improperly serving on the boards of competing artificial intelligence companies, according to people familiar with the matter.
articles.author: Josh Sisco and Natasha Mascarenhas

articles.title: Groq Valued at $3.5 Billion in Funding Round After Nvidia Deal
articles.summary: Groq has raised $350 million in funding at a $3.5 billion valuation, roughly half what it was worth nearly a year ago before Nvidia Corp. struck a licensing deal with the startup and hired away much of its talent.The financing, set to be announced Monday, was led by Dallas-based investment firm Disruptive. articles.title: HSG-Backed Robotera Is Said to Mull HK IPO as Robot Tech Booms
articles.summary: Robotera, a Chinese robotics startup backed by HSG and CDH Investments, is planning an initial public offering in Hong Kong, people familiar with the matter said, as a growing number of companies in the industry look to go public.
